finding: F6D-08; the F2-06 D review, benign column
case: The same five computed projections, in reverse order.
why: The table is a SET of records nothing may write, and every check over it is a membership check. A control that refused a reordering would be refusing an edit that changes no record's command list, and a control contributors learn to route around protects nothing -- the argument this package makes at r20, r30 and r32.

value.why: The operator's view is computed from the records it projects; writing it directly would make the view and the thing disagree with nothing noticing.
Status is read off the operation's own lifecycle. A writable status is a report of success for work that stopped, which is W7's failure condition verbatim.
Events are emitted by the kernel commit path, never registered through a record command; a permitted command here would let a party author its own history.
The reachability closure over access grants is derived from the grants; a command that wrote it would let a component grant itself reach.

`05` section 7: a computed projection with no lifecycle that nobody writes, and in particular the admission authority holds no write access to any precondition-bearing kind. m4 is the mutation this row refuses.
